原发与转移性鼻咽癌基因组和免疫差异的纵向分析：面向精准肿瘤学

Longitudinal analysis of genomic and immune differences between primary and metastatic nasopharyngeal carcinoma for precision oncology.

中文摘要

鼻咽癌（NPC）是一种常见恶性肿瘤，在中国南方和东南亚地区发病率高。远处转移仍是预后不良的主要原因。本研究旨在通过纵向分析探讨原发性和转移性NPC的基因组和免疫微环境变化，为指导精准治疗策略提供见解。 我们分析了11例伴有远处转移的男性NPC患者的肿瘤样本。配對的原发和转移样本接受了靶向全外显子组测序（551个基因）和RNA测序（289个基因）。采用多重免疫组化评估免疫细胞组成和免疫反应标志物。比较原发性和转移性肿瘤之间的基因组改变和免疫特征，并评估其与临床结局的关联。 转移性肿瘤表现出独特的染色体改变，包括频繁的1q增益，而6p增益显示出延长生存的趋势。原发性肿瘤表现出更强的免疫抑制，其特征是B细胞和Treg浸润增加以及CTLA4和IDO1表达升高，而转移性病变则显示出更活跃的免疫反应。肝转移呈现出独特的免疫景观，与非肝转移相比，CD8+ T细胞密度较低。在局部晚期NPC中，EGFR和MYC等致癌基因的高表达与较短的无病生存期相关，而PANCK表达升高和细胞毒性增强则与更好的结局相关。这些结果描绘了NPC的分子和免疫演化，为开发精准治疗策略提供了基础。 本研究确定了与NPC生存相关的关键分子和免疫特征。原发性肿瘤显示出免疫抑制表型，提示联合CTLA4或IDO1抑制剂与PD-1阻断可能获益。肝转移表现出独特的免疫特征，支持需要部位特异性精准治疗。这些发现有助于NPC的个性化管理策略，根据分子和免疫特征指导治疗。

英文摘要

Nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC) is a common malignancy with a high incidence in Southern China and Southeast Asia. Distant metastasis remains a major cause of poor prognosis. This study aims to explore the genomic and immune microenvironmental changes in primary and metastatic NPC through longitudinal analysis, to provide insights for guiding precision treatment strategies. We analyzed tumor samples from 11 male NPC patients with distant metastasis. Paired primary and metastatic samples underwent targeted whole-exome sequencing (551 genes) and RNA sequencing (289 genes). Multiplex immunohistochemistry was performed to assess immune cell composition and immune response markers. Genomic alterations and immune features were compared between primary and metastatic tumors, and their associations with clinical outcomes were evaluated. Metastatic tumors exhibited distinct chromosomal changes, including frequent 1q gain, while 6p gain showed a trend toward prolonged survival. Primary tumors showed stronger immune suppression characterized by increased B-cell and Treg infiltration and elevated CTLA4 and IDO1 expression, whereas metastatic lesions displayed more active immune responses. Liver metastases presented a distinct immune landscape with lower CD8+ T-cell density compared to non-liver metastases. In locoregionally advanced NPC, high expression of oncogenic genes such as EGFR and MYC correlated with shorter disease-free survival, while elevated PANCK expression and enhanced cytotoxicity were linked to better outcomes. These results delineate the molecular and immune evolution of NPC and provide a foundation for developing precision therapeutic strategies. This study identifies key molecular and immune features associated with NPC survival. Primary tumors show an immunosuppressive phenotype, suggesting potential benefits from combining CTLA4 or IDO1 inhibitors with PD-1 blockade. Liver metastases exhibit distinct immune features, supporting the need for site-specific precision therapies. These findings contribute to personalized management strategies in NPC, guiding treatment based on molecular and immune profiles.
